title: How to harvest okra
seoTitle: How to Harvest Okra: When to Pick and How Often
description: Pick okra pods at 2 to 4 inches, every day or two, before they turn woody. Why to use pruners and gloves, and how to store and eat your harvest.
summary: Pick okra pods when they're about 2 to 4 inches long, and pick every day or two. A pod goes from just right to too big in about 2 days, and regular picking keeps the plant producing.

intro: Okra rewards the gardener who shows up. Once the plants start producing, there are new pods ready almost every day, and in our garden a pod goes from just right to too big in about 2 days.
New to okra? Start with [how to grow okra](/okra/how-to-grow-okra), or get [free okra seeds](/okra/free-okra-seeds) from Olivia's garden.

items: First pods about 2 months after planting
Pick at about 2 to 4 inches long
Cut with pruners, and wear gloves
Store unwashed, rinse before eating, and use within about 3 days

blocks.text: Okra plants [flower about 2 months after planting](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/gardening/okra/), and each pod is ready to pick 3 to 4 days after its flower opens. Smaller pods are the most tender. Clemson Extension notes that [2 to 3 inch pods are still tender](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/), while bigger pods get tougher and more fibrous.

blocks.title: From Olivia's garden
blocks.text: We pick our Clemson Spineless pods anywhere from 2 to 5 inches long. Past that they turn woody, and it happens fast. A pod goes from a good size to too big in about 2 days.

Pick every day or two. Texas A&M AgriLife warns that if you don't pick [every 1 to 2 days, yields will decrease](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/gardening/okra/), and Clemson Extension advises not letting pods mature on the plant, since that slows down new pods.

Picked often and kept watered, okra can keep producing [for up to 12 weeks](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/), and in a long, hot summer it often goes until frost.

sections.title: How to cut okra, and why to wear gloves

items: Put on gloves. Okra pods and stems are covered in tiny hairs that get stuck in your hands.

Cut each pod off with [pruners or a sharp knife](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/). The plant is so fibrous that pods don't snap off cleanly by hand.
Handle the pods gently. They bruise easily.
Check the whole plant every time you pick, so no pod gets left long enough to turn woody.

sections.title: Okra pods too big or woody

blocks.text: Pods that grew too long are tough and stringy, and cooking won't soften them. Even our goats and chickens turn their noses up at overgrown okra.
So we leave them on the plant. They keep maturing until they dry and split, and then we [harvest the seeds](/okra/saving-okra-seeds) for next year.

blocks.alt: A small, tender okra pod at picking size below an overgrown pod about three times as long, laid on a linen cloth.
blocks.caption: A pod at picking size (bottom) next to an overgrown one (top).

sections.title: How to store and eat fresh okra

blocks.text: Fresh okra doesn't keep long. Texas A&M AgriLife says it lasts [3 to 5 days in the refrigerator](https://agrilifeextension.tamu.edu/library/gardening/okra/), and ours is best within about 3 days of picking, so pick close to when you'll eat it. Don't wash the pods until you're ready to use them, since washing [speeds up decay](https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/how-to-grow-okra-in-south-carolina-including-planting-dates-watering-fertilizing-ratooning-pest-management-and-harvesting-tips-for-healthy-pod-production/). To keep okra longer, see [how to preserve okra](/okra/preserving-okra).

We love okra fresh from the garden, as well as pickled, stir-fried with other vegetables, and of course fried. Whichever way you eat it, rinse the pods under running water just before eating or cooking.

faq.question: How big should okra be when you pick it?
faq.answer: About 2 to 4 inches long, and smaller pods are the most tender. We pick our Clemson Spineless up to 5 inches, but past that they turn tough and woody.

faq.question: Why is my okra tough and woody?
faq.answer: It stayed on the plant too long. A pod can go from a good size to too big in about 2 days, so pick every day or two to keep up.

faq.question: Do you need gloves to pick okra?
faq.answer: We recommend them. Okra pods and stems are covered in tiny hairs that get stuck in your hands, and pruners give a cleaner cut than snapping pods off.

faq.question: How often should you harvest okra?
faq.answer: Every day or two once the plants start producing. Regular picking keeps the plant making new pods.

faq.question: Can you eat okra raw?
faq.answer: Yes. We love eating young, tender pods fresh from the garden. Rinse them under running water first.
